_README: Cost and accuracy figures for memory systems as REPORTED by their own
papers. Nothing here was measured by this repo.
Every entry was checked against the actual paper on 2026-07-29 and carries
`verified: true` with the specific table it came from, or was removed.
Caution that must survive into any plot or table: these were measured on
different benchmarks (LoCoMo for Mem0/RecMem, LongMemEval for the energy
numbers) and are NOT directly comparable to each other or to our measured
numbers. Label the benchmark on every number you display.

_removed.claim: verbatim RAG costs ~$0.01 with no LLM calls while Mem0 costs $0.50+ with 1000+ LLM calls per instance
_removed.note: That paper quantifies construction cost in energy (kJ) and LLM call counts, not dollars. No such dollar figures appear. The claim came from a search-result paraphrase and should never be cited.
Mem0's own Table 2 reports 72.90 +/- 0.19 for the full-context baseline. The 70.71 figure came from a secondary discussion, not a primary table.

locomo_read_path._unit: mean retrieved-memory tokens placed in the answering model's context per question (Table 2's 'chunk size / memory tokens' column)
locomo_read_path._comparability: This counts retrieved context only, not the surrounding prompt template or the question. This repo's read-path figures are measured the same way, so the two are like-for-like; adding this repo's ~500-token template to both sides would move the full-context ratio from 49.6x to about 40x.
locomo_read_path._note: This paper reports NO write-path cost. It documents retrieval and inference latency but is silent on tokens or LLM calls consumed during memory extraction and consolidation. That omission is the gap this repo is about.

locomo_construction_tokens._note: Secondary source for Mem0 and A-Mem: these are RecMem's measurements of its competitors, not those systems' own reported figures. Mem0's own paper does not report this at all, so no primary source exists.
locomo_construction_tokens._extraction_model_matters: Table 1 reports each system under two extraction models. Pair the token count with the price of the SAME model. This repo prices at gpt-4o-mini, so it uses the gpt-4o-mini column; quoting the gpt-4.1-mini token count at gpt-4o-mini prices would overstate the build cost by 23%.

longmemeval_construction_tokens._note: Same benchmark this repo measures on, so this is the most directly comparable published construction figure for Mem0 that exists. Still a competitor's measurement, not Mem0's own.

longmemeval_construction_energy._source: Agent Memory: Characterization and System Implications of Stateful Long-Horizon Workloads, arXiv 2606.06448, Table 3
longmemeval_construction_energy._unit: kilojoules end-to-end; llm_calls covers construction + 300 QA calls
longmemeval_construction_energy._note: Same benchmark this repo uses, so the relative ordering is the most comparable published evidence available. The paper's Section 4.2 is titled 'Construction Dominates the Agent Lifecycle'. It classifies BM25/embedRAG as Paradigm II: deterministic indexing with no LLM calls.
longmemeval_construction_energy._reading_the_calls_column: Table 3's Calls column is construction + 300 QA. BM25's 300 is therefore one call per query and zero construction. Subtract 300 to approximate construction calls: Mem0 ~4,238, GraphRAG ~2,915, Letta ~18,094.
longmemeval_construction_energy._accuracy_caveat: Table 3 also reports accuracy, where Mem0 scores 32.0 against BM25's 47.0. That is a different generator and setup from Mem0's own paper and is not a like-for-like restatement of it.

mem0_2026_algorithm._source: Mem0, 'The Token-Efficient Memory Algorithm', mem0.ai blog, 2026
mem0_2026_algorithm._source_type: vendor blog post, not peer reviewed
mem0_2026_algorithm._note: Recorded because the 2025 paper no longer describes Mem0's default path. Extraction is single-pass and ADD-only -- UPDATE and DELETE are gone, superseded facts coexist -- and retrieval fuses semantic, keyword and entity matching. That makes the write path cheaper than the paper's two-phase design, though still at least one LLM call per message pair. Quoted in README.md as Mem0's own reported figures, not as a measurement by this repo.

judge_reliability._source: Same Ranking, Different Winner: How Scoring Targets Shape LLM Memory Benchmarks, arXiv 2605.24060
judge_reliability._note: Peer-reviewable evidence that judged scores on these benchmarks are sensitive to a free choice the grader makes. This is the citation the judge-free design rests on.

locomo_answer_key_audit._source_type: non-peer-reviewed vendor blog post, not a paper
locomo_answer_key_audit._note: Previously quoted in this repo as though it were a paper. It is a vendor audit with public artifacts. Cite it only with that label, and never as the sole support for a claim. This repo's own measured judge result (below) is stronger evidence and needs no external source.

_measured_here_not_published._note: For contrast with everything above: the grader error rates this repo reports are measured by scripts/audit_graders.py and re-measured by CI on every push. They are not quoted from anyone.
